text: Automation drives wage divergence: as routine tasks are automated, wages stagnate or fall for workers in exposed roles while wages rise for workers in high skill non routine jobs, which widens income inequality.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Quantum Economy and the Future of Work (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4900880

isBasedOn.name: Quantum Economy and the Future of Work

abstract: As routine tasks become increasingly automated, there's a risk of wage stagnation or even decline for workers in roles susceptible to automation. At the same time, those in high-skill, non-routine jobs may see their wages increase, potentially exacerbating income inequality.
